Codex review: needs real behavior proof before merge. ## What this changes This PR moves bundled session mutations through worker-backed SDK operations while preserving released compatibility adapters. **Example:** A plugin renames session agent:main:managed to Research. - **Before:** A promise-returning mutation can still perform SQLite work on the Gateway thread. - **After:** Preparation runs outside SQLite, and the owning worker conditionally commits Research with the applicable authority checks. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | The implementation follows existing owners and preserves compatibility, but final-effect authority validation limits readiness. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Real behavior proof is necessary before merge. See [Before merge](#before-merge). | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Security review found an item that needs attention. | ## Product **Kind:** Refactor · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Session persistence can occupy the Gateway thread, and queued mutations can outlive the plugin capability that authorized them. **Reason:** Maintainer direction and merged feature history support consolidating persistence through existing worker owners while retaining shipped contracts. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 4 items remain** Keep this useful maintainer-directed PR open; no discrete introduced bug was established, and the earlier conflict blocker is resolved. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `2223b22b14ee08b0ee16135be7816f906c3469c2` ## Before merge - [ ] **Add real behavior proof** - Authority-chain proof required: supplied built-runtime measurements support the worker migration, but add redacted logs or terminal output showing allowed patches, upserts, and routes committing through the actual scoped runtime and SQLite writer while foreign or retired plugins leave storage unchanged, including retirement after preparation before commit; redact credentials, IPs, phone numbers, and non-public endpoints. After adding proof, update the PR body; ClawSweeper should re-review automatically. If it does not, the PR author or someone with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. - [ ] **Resolve security concern: Verify managed authority through the final storage effect** - The retirement cases replace persistence methods, while real-worker cases supply host authority directly; their production composition has not demonstrated rejection before SQLite commit. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk** - Queued mutations carry managed-plugin authority across preparation and worker admission; rejection of foreign or retired plugins at the final storage effect remains unproven. - [ ] **Complete next step** - Have the landing owner classify failures in the exact-head CI run against its tested base before applying an inherited-failure exception. ## Findings - [medium] Verify managed authority through the final storage effect — `src/plugins/registry.runtime-session-ownership.test.ts:49` ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: Show allowed, foreign-owner, and post-preparation retirement cases through the real scoped plugin runtime and SQLite writer, with final persisted-state observations.
Agent review details ### How this fits together Plugin and channel callers submit session changes through the SDK; database workers commit SQLite state and publish committed facts to runtime consumers. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Bundled callers] --> B[Scoped plugin runtime] B --> C[Session SDK] C --> D[Preparation and authority] D --> E[Database worker] E --> F[SQLite session state] E --> G[Committed facts] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Complete the existing worker-owner cutover while preserving released adapters and demonstrating final-effect plugin authority. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Current-main source retains native callback compatibility paths that can perform caller-thread SQLite work; this read-only review ran no reproduction. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Reusing the existing worker, exact-snapshot commit, and publication owners is appropriate, with explicitly retained compatibility boundaries. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Confidence: 0.98 What I checked: - **Verified introduced behavior:** The pinned introduction adds prepared patches, conditional data patches, authority-bound routes, and bundled caller migrations through existing storage owners. ([`src/plugin-sdk/session-store-runtime.ts:270`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2223b22b14ee08b0ee16135be7816f906c3469c2/src/plugin-sdk/session-store-runtime.ts#L270), [2223b22b14ee](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2223b22b14ee08b0ee16135be7816f906c3469c2)) - **Current-main boundary:** Fetched main retains the callback SDK implementation without the prepared replacement introduced here; the central cutover remains distinct work. ([`src/plugin-sdk/session-store-runtime.ts:229`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/171df4e1c5a08e1da631c4fff50c420db2bb6f84/src/plugin-sdk/session-store-runtime.ts#L229), [171df4e1c5a0](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/171df4e1c5a08e1da631c4fff50c420db2bb6f84)) - **Authority evidence boundary:** Managed-plugin retirement tests substitute preparation and route persistence with local-variable writes; separate SDK tests exercise the real worker using directly supplied host authority. ([`src/plugins/registry.runtime-session-ownership.test.ts:49`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2223b22b14ee08b0ee16135be7816f906c3469c2/src/plugins/registry.runtime-session-ownership.test.ts#L49), [2223b22b14ee](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2223b22b14ee08b0ee16135be7816f906c3469c2)) - **Complete proof account inspected:** The complete REST body, including omitted excerpts, reports built-runtime workload measurements and a v2026.9.9-driver update preserving durable and incognito content on 808c7b409ec57e201f8cd01f744a3a8c3dbbfba6; it does not demonstrate the complete managed-plugin authority scenario. ([2223b22b14ee](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2223b22b14ee08b0ee16135be7816f906c3469c2)) - **Released compatibility:** Legacy callbacks and synchronous adapters remain available, with documented replacements and removal at the next Plugin SDK major: https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-migration/how-to-migrate#prepare-session-entry-changes. ([`docs/plugins/sdk-migration/how-to-migrate.md:248`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-migration/how-to-migrate), [2223b22b14ee](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2223b22b14ee08b0ee16135be7816f906c3469c2)) - **Accepted retained boundaries:** The maintainer-authored body explicitly retains process-held incognito and cross-store atomic adapters pending separate cutovers and acknowledges the additional transport cost of prepared transcript operations. Public docs: [`docs/reference/database-schemas/worker-access.md`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/database-schemas/worker-access).
